nodes.description: Amblyopia is a recognised visual risk of chalazion-induced astigmatism in young children.

evidence.snippet: visual symptoms such as refractive errors and amblyopia in children, blurred vision secondary to induced astigmatism or mechanical ptosis

nodes.description: Chalazion-induced astigmatism, more common with lesions in the middle of the upper lid, larger lesions and two lesions. In children aged 0.5 to 6 years the incidence was 40.29% with a single chalazion and 49.31% with multiple chalazia; frequency is not set because these figures come from a young paediatric cohort only.

evidence.reference_title: Multivariate analysis of the effect of Chalazia on astigmatism in children.
evidence.snippet: Chalazia in children can easily lead to astigmatism, especially AR and OBL.

evidence.reference_title: Multivariate analysis of the effect of Chalazia on astigmatism in children.
evidence.snippet: The incidence rate of astigmatism was significantly higher in the multiple chalazion group (49.31%) than in the single chalazion group (40.29%).

nodes.description: Vision can blur from induced astigmatism or mechanical ptosis.

nodes.description: A firm, slowly enlarging, usually non-tender nodule within the eyelid. It is more often in the upper than the lower lid; in a series of 471 paediatric eyes the upper lid was affected in 56.9%.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence and risk factors for chalazion in an older veteran population.
evidence.snippet: Typically slow-growing, non-tender, and nodular, chalazia are considered to be the most common inflammatory eyelid lesion in the general population today.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features, treatment outcomes, and risk factors for surgery in pediatric chalazion.
evidence.snippet: The upper eyelid was affected in the majority (56.9%), followed by the lower lid (33.3%), with involvement of both lids in 5.9%.

nodes.description: The affected eyelid is swollen. Lid swelling was the presenting complaint in 24% of a paediatric series; that series is children only, so no frequency band is set.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features, treatment outcomes, and risk factors for surgery in pediatric chalazion.
evidence.snippet: Regarding clinical symptoms, boil-like lesions were the most common complaint (34.6%), followed by lid swelling (24%).

nodes.description: Some lesions are tender, usually while still actively inflamed; most established chalazia are painless. Eye pain was recorded in 8.1% of a paediatric series.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of Care and Antibiotic Use for Chalazia and Hordeola.
evidence.snippet: A chalazion is a benign eyelid lesion associated with blepharitis that typically presents as a subacute tender nodule arising from an obstructed meibomian gland characterized by lipogranulomatous inflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features, treatment outcomes, and risk factors for surgery in pediatric chalazion.

nodes.description: Transconjunctival incision and curettage under local anaesthesia after failed conservative care. It has the highest single-procedure success and lower recurrence than steroid injection, and it yields tissue for histopathology. Thermal cautery after surgery did not change recurrence. Children often need general anaesthesia for the procedure.

evidence.reference_title: Incision and Curettage Versus Steroid Injection for the Treatment of Chalazia: A Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: There were 264 patients treated by I&C with a larger aggregate success rate of 78.0% with 1 procedure and 86.7% with 1 or 2 procedures (p < 0.05 for both comparisons).

evidence.reference_title: A prospective randomized study comparing incision and curettage with injection of triamcinolone acetonide for chronic chalazia.
evidence.snippet: Advantages of I&C in comparison to TA include less recurrence, shorter duration of complications, and a higher success rate.

evidence.reference_title: Thermal cautery after chalazion surgery and its effect on recurrence rates.
evidence.snippet: The results of this clinical study suggest that the use of thermal cautery with surgery has no impact on the recurrence rate of internal chalazia.

evidence.reference_title: Epidemiology and associated factors of childhood chalazion in China: a seven-year, hospital-based, multicenter, cross-sectional study.
evidence.snippet: Of 117,009 pediatric ophthalmic procedures performed under general anesthesia, 33,489 (28.62 %) were chalazion excisions.

nodes.description: Intralesional corticosteroid injection is an alternative to incision and curettage after failed conservative care. Single-injection success is lower than after one incision and curettage, and recurrence was higher in one trial; the gap narrows when a second injection is allowed. Skin depigmentation is relatively common in pigmented skin, and eyelid fat atrophy with depigmentation has been reported in young children. Injection avoids a tissue specimen, so it suits lesions whose diagnosis is not in doubt.

evidence.reference_title: Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide injection versus incision and curettage for primary chalazia: a prospective, randomized study.
evidence.snippet: Complete resolution was achieved in 33 (79%) of 42 patients in the I&C group and in 42 (81%) of 52 patients in the TA group (P=.8, chi-square analysis).

evidence.reference_title: Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide injection versus incision and curettage for primary chalazia: a prospective, randomized study.
evidence.snippet: Injection may be considered as an alternative first-line treatment in cases where diagnosis is straightforward and no biopsy is required.

evidence.reference_title: Incision and Curettage Versus Steroid Injection for the Treatment of Chalazia: A Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: This analysis shows that I&C is more effective than SI with 1 procedure. This benefit is reduced when comparing 1 or 2 attempts of I&C and SI.

evidence.reference_title: A prospective randomized study comparing incision and curettage with injection of triamcinolone acetonide for chronic chalazia.
evidence.snippet: Lesion recurrence occurred in 9 patients (34.61%) in the TA group and 2 (8%) in the I&C (P = 0.04).

evidence.reference_title: Intralesional corticosteroid injection vs surgical treatment of chalazia in pigmented patients.
evidence.snippet: It is not associated with any serious complications although skin depigmentation is relatively common in coloured population.

evidence.reference_title: Eyelid Fat Atrophy and Depigmentation After an Intralesional Injection of Triamcinolone Acetonide to Treat Chalazion.
evidence.snippet: Two patients with depigmentation and fat atrophy after an intralesional injection of triamcinolone acetonide (TA) to treat chalazion are reported.

nodes.description: A chronic lipogranuloma with a predominantly T-cell infiltrate, in which CD4-positive T cells outnumber CD8-positive T cells, forms around the lipid inside a fibrous pseudocapsule and produces the firm eyelid nodule.

evidence.reference_title: Differentiation between chalazion and sebaceous carcinoma by noninvasive meibography.
evidence.snippet: Histopathologically, chalazion manifests as a lipogranulomatous reaction to liberated lipid granules contained within a connective tissue pseudocapsule.

evidence.reference_title: Immunophenotypic profiles in chalazion and pyogenic granuloma associated with chalazion.
evidence.snippet: The chalazion and pyogenic granuloma lesions shared similar immunophenotypic profile characterized by predominant T cell infiltration, and CD4 T cells dominating over CD8 cells.

nodes.description: Lower serum vitamin A has been reported in children and adolescents with chalazion, and was lowest in recurrent, multiple chalazia. Evidence comes from a single small case-control study.

evidence.reference_title: Serum Vitamin A Levels in Patients with Chalazion.
evidence.snippet: Serum vitamin A levels in patients with recurrent, multiple chalazia were significantly lower than in patients with primary, multiple chalazia (P = 0.026) and patients with a recurrent, single chalazion (P = 0.029).

nodes.description: Pressure from a large upper-lid chalazion deforms the cornea and changes its topography.

evidence.reference_title: Effects of chalazia on corneal astigmatism : Large-sized chalazia in middle upper eyelids compress the cornea and induce the corneal astigmatism.
evidence.snippet: Astigmatism by simK, second order aberration, oblique astigmatism, and vertical astigmatism were significantly greater in the large-sized chalazion group (p < 0.05).

nodes.description: Noninfectious obstruction of the meibomian (or Zeis) gland duct in the tarsal plate retains the gland's lipid secretion.

evidence.reference_title: Differentiation between chalazion and sebaceous carcinoma by noninvasive meibography.
evidence.snippet: It often arises secondarily to noninfectious obstruction of a meibomian gland duct.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence and risk factors for chalazion in an older veteran population.
evidence.snippet: Chalazia are inflammatory nodules that develop on the eyelid surface as a result of lipogranulomatous inflammation secondary to tarsal plate Meibomian gland duct obstruction.

nodes.description: Chronic disease of the eyelid margin and periocular skin, including blepharitis, meibomian gland dysfunction and rosacea, is the strongest recognised substrate for chalazion and for multiple or recurrent lesions.
nodes.id: Meibomian Gland Dysfunction and Lid-Margin Disease

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence and risk factors for chalazion in an older veteran population.
evidence.snippet: Periocular skin, eyelid margin and tear film abnormalities were most strongly associated with risk for chalazion.

evidence.reference_title: Associated morbidity of chalazia.
evidence.snippet: The following risk factors of chalazion were statistically significant: blepharitis

evidence.reference_title: Chalazion: racial risk factors for formation, recurrence, and surgical intervention.
evidence.snippet: More than one chalazion was recorded in 31% of subjects without coexisting meibomian gland disease, blepharitis, or marginal keratitis, and in 56% (p < 0.0001) with one of these conditions.

evidence.reference_title: Risk Factors for Chalazion Diagnosis and Subsequent Surgical Excision.
evidence.snippet: Female sex, non-white race, conditions affecting periocular skin and the tear film, several non-ocular inflammatory conditions, and smoking were risk factors for chalazion diagnosis.

nodes.description: Demodex folliculorum and Demodex brevis eyelash and gland infestation is more common in people with chalazion and is linked to recurrent and multiple lesions. It is recorded as an association and risk factor, not as a causal agent; the histopathology study that found more D. folliculorum in chalazion-bearing lids could not establish causality.

evidence.reference_title: The association of demodex infestation with pediatric chalazia.
evidence.snippet: Demodex was found in 236 (52.91%) patients with chalazia and zero control patients.

evidence.reference_title: The association of demodex infestation with pediatric chalazia.
evidence.snippet: Demodex infestation was more prevalent in pediatric chalazia patients than healthy children, and was associated with recurrent and multiple chalazia.

evidence.reference_title: Ocular demodicidosis as a risk factor of adult recurrent chalazion.
evidence.snippet: Among 48 eyes with recurrent chalazion, Demodex mites were found in 35 (72.9%).

evidence.reference_title: Demodex mites as potential etiological factor in chalazion - a study in Poland.
evidence.snippet: Demodex was detected in 91.67% of patients with a chalazion.

nodes.description: A large lesion can weigh the lid down and cause mechanical ptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Multivariate analysis of the effect of Chalazia on astigmatism in children.
evidence.snippet: A chalazion causes swelling of the eyelids and ptosis and can develop in children and adults.

nodes.description: Retained and liberated meibomian lipid acts as an indigestible foreign-body stimulus that sustains chronic, sterile inflammation around the gland.

evidence.reference_title: A prospective randomized study comparing incision and curettage with injection of triamcinolone acetonide for chronic chalazia.
evidence.snippet: Chalazion is a common chronic sterile lipogranulomatous mass in the eyelid that is the result of obstruction of the meibomian glands.

evidence.reference_title: Meibum and lid margin microbiome in eyes with chalazion: exploring an infectious aetiology.
evidence.snippet: None of the culture media (for aerobic, anaerobic bacteria and fungus) showed any bacterial growth.

nodes.description: In adults with recurrent chalazion and confirmed ocular Demodex, weekly 50% tea tree oil lid scrubs with daily tea tree shampoo scrubs were associated with few recurrences. The study was retrospective and had no control group.
nodes.id: Tea tree oil lid scrubs for Demodex-associated recurrence

evidence.reference_title: Ocular demodicidosis as a risk factor of adult recurrent chalazion.
evidence.snippet: Among the treatment group, all cases except one had no recurrence after the TTO treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Ocular demodicidosis as a risk factor of adult recurrent chalazion.
evidence.snippet: The study is limited by the lack of a control group.

nodes.description: Smoking is a modest but consistent risk factor for chalazion in case-control and cohort studies.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence and risk factors for chalazion in an older veteran population.
evidence.snippet: Factors associated with chalazion risk included smoking (OR=1.12, p<0.0005)

evidence.reference_title: Risk Factors for Chalazion Diagnosis and Subsequent Surgical Excision.
evidence.snippet: Female sex, non-white race, conditions affecting periocular skin and the tear film, several non-ocular inflammatory conditions, and smoking were risk factors for chalazion diagnosis.

nodes.description: First-line conservative care with warm compresses, lid massage and lid hygiene. Most lesions resolve, though resolution within a few weeks is lower than after a procedure; adding topical tobramycin or tobramycin-dexamethasone to hot compresses did not improve resolution in a randomized trial. Conservative care succeeds most often in young children with small lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Conservative therapy for chalazia: is it really effective?
evidence.snippet: Hot compresses (HC) alone or in combination with tobramycin or tobramycin/dexamethasone drops and ointment are all effective first-line treatment options for chalazia.

evidence.reference_title: A prospective randomized treatment study comparing three treatment options for chalazia: triamcinolone acetonide injections, incision and curettage and treatment with hot compresses.
evidence.snippet: At the 3-week follow up, the resolution rates in the triamcinolone acetonide injection and surgical treatment groups were not significantly different from each other at 84% (47/56) and 87% (39/45), respectively (P < 0.001), but was significantly lower in the conservative treatment group at 46% (16/35) (P < 0.001).

evidence.reference_title: Conservative Treatment of Chalazion in Pediatric Patients.
evidence.snippet: The success rate of conservative treatment was 85.7% (78/91): 96.7% (29/30) in group A, 86.8% (33/38) in group B, and 69.7% (16/23) in group C (P = 0.022).
